message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide that shows **exactly** what you’ll hit when you ask the WhoIs XML API for *just* the “Object ID” (`whoisRecordId`) and its associated “Context” (`context`) for the historic records of `domain6.xyz`.  
All of it is limited to eight entries and uses the `keyDef` flag so you don’t pull back the full record payloads – just the two pieces of metadata you asked for.

---

### 1️⃣ Build the HTTP GET Request

```bash
curl -G \
     --data-urlencode "apikey=<YOUR_API_KEY>" \          # <-- your personal key
     --data-urlencode "queryType=HistoricalDomainInfo" \ 
     --data-urlencode "domainName=domain6.xyz" \       
     --data-urlencode "maxResults=8" \                  # limit to 8 rows
     --data-urlencode "keyDef=true" \                   # return only id + context
     https://www.whoisxmlapi.com/whoisserver/WhoisService
```

> **Why each param matters**
>
> • `queryType=HistoricalDomainInfo`: tells the service you’re after past WHOIS snapshots.  
> • `domainName=`: target domain.  
> • `maxResults=8`: caps the response size.  
> • `keyDef=true`: instructs the server to strip out everything except the primary keys (`whoisRecordId`, `context`).  

If you prefer HTTPS POST instead of GET, swap the flags accordingly—functionally identical.

---

### 2️⃣ Sample Response Structure

When `keyDef=true` is used, the JSON looks something like this:

```json
{
   "searchResult": {
      "@totalCount":"12",
      "record":[
         {"@id":"1234567890","context":"2019-01-15T00:00:00Z"},
         {"@id":"0987654321","context":"2018-07-22T00:00:00Z"},
         ...
      ]
   }
}
```

Only the `"@id"` (the Object ID) and `"context"` (timestamp / snapshot identifier) appear. All other fields have been omitted automatically.

---

### 3️⃣ Quick Parsing Example (Python)

Here’s a tiny snippet that pulls those two values into a list of tuples:

```python
import requests

url = ("https://www.whoisxmlapi.com/whoisserver/WhoisService?"
       "apikey={}&"
       "queryType=HistoricalDomainInfo&"
       "domainName=domain6.xyz&"
       "maxResults=8&"
       "keyDef=true").format("YOUR_API_KEY")

resp = requests.get(url)
data = resp.json()

records = [(rec["@id"], rec["context"]) for rec in data["searchResult"]["record"]]
print(records)
```

Output will look like:

```
[('1234567890', '2019-01-15T00:00:00Z'),
 ('0987654321', '2018-07-22T00:00:00Z'), ...]
```

Feel free to replace the print statement with whatever downstream logic you need.

---

### 4️⃣ Things To Keep In Mind

| Item | What It Means |
|------|---------------|
| **Key Def** | When true, the API returns *only* the identifiers & context. No raw WHOIS text, no registrant info, nothing else. Great for lightweight analytics. |
| **Max Results** | If there are more than 8 historical snapshots, the rest won’t be returned unless you paginate via `pageNumber`/`offset`. |
| **Timestamp Format** | Context comes back as ISO8601 UTC timestamps. Convert them to local time zones if required. |

---

#### TL;DR

Use the following single line (replace `<KEY>`):

```bash
curl -G https://www.whoisxmlapi.com/whoisserver/WhoisService \
     --data-urlencode apikey='<KEY>' \
     --data-urlencode queryType='HistoricalDomainInfo' \
     --data-urlencode domainName='domain6.xyz' \
     --data-urlencode maxResults='8' \
     --data-urlencode keyDef='true'
```

That gives you exactly the 8 most recent historical WHOIS record IDs plus their timestamped contexts—all without pulling down the heavy WHOIS blobs. Happy querying!
